column2: The Lord addresses both Moses and Aaron for the purification law.
The red heifer must be unblemished, without defect and never yoked. The repeated blemish restriction is retained.
Eleazar receives the animal; unnamed others take it outside to a clean place and slaughter before him. The selected clean-place clause remains.
Eleazar sprinkles blood seven times toward the tent front. No finger instruction absent from this selected verse is inserted.
Skin, flesh, blood and dung all burn before Eleazar. The list is not reduced to selected animal parts.
The priest takes cedar, hyssop and scarlet material, then plural they throw them into the burning. The agent-number shift remains.
The priest washes clothing and body before entering camp, while remaining unclean until evening. Entry is not delayed until after that evening by the English.
The burner also washes clothes and body and remains unclean until evening.
A clean person stores the ashes outside in a clean place for Israel's sprinkling water. Means of purification retains the selected purification noun.
The ash gatherer washes clothes and becomes unclean until evening; the enduring rule includes attached sojourners.
Touching any human corpse causes seven-day impurity. Human being is explicit rather than extending the rule to every animal corpse here.
Third- and seventh-day purification are both required; omission of both named occasions leaves the person unclean.
The unpurified corpse-toucher defiles the tent and is wiped out from Israel. The absent sprinkling and impurity still in him are both retained.
The selected setting is a house, not a tent. All entering and all contents share seven-day impurity.
An open vessel without a tied fastening is unclean. No particular lid material is invented.
On the open plain the listed contacts are slain person, dead person, human bone and tomb; all lead to seven days.
column3: Slain is the provisional contextual sense of the wounded-person term in this corpse-purity list.

column2: Ashes of the burned purification material receive living water in a vessel. The unnamed preparers remain plural.
The proposal uses upon for the house, vessels and people, preserving the objects receiving sprinkling rather than placing it around them. The four contact categories remain complete.
A clean person sprinkles on days three and seven; purification, washing and bathing follow, with uncleanness until evening explicitly retained.
Failure to purify brings destruction from the assembly because holy things were defiled; absent sprinkling explains continued impurity.
The sprinkler washes clothes, while touching the water brings impurity until evening. The two roles and requirements remain distinct.
An unclean person's touch transfers impurity to an object and then to its toucher until evening. The chain is retained.
The whole congregation arrives in the first month; Miriam dies and is buried at Kadesh. No year is supplied.
column3: Zin is an inherited conventional rendering of Greek Sin here, unlike the spelling at 13:21; geographic name normalization remains unapproved.

column2: Lack of water prompts assembly against Moses and Aaron.
The people revile Moses and wish they had died with the previously destroyed brothers. No particular earlier episode is named in the verse.
They accuse the leaders of bringing congregation and livestock to death; both human and animal objects remain.
The complaint lists no sowing, figs, vines, pomegranates or drinking water. All lacks remain.
Moses and Aaron leave the assembly for the tent entrance, fall down and receive the appearance of glory.
The divine instruction is addressed to Moses.
Taking the staff and assembling the congregation lead to a plural command to speak to the rock. The rock gives water for people and livestock.
Moses takes the staff from before the Lord; no ownership of that staff is added.
Both leaders assemble the people, followed by a singular speaker and a negative rhetorical question. Disobedient remains the address.
column3: The negative question's English force needs fuller review; the draft does not resolve its doubt, challenge or rhetorical intent into commentary.

column2: Moses strikes twice, and abundant water supplies congregation and livestock. Twice is preserved against the prior command to speak.
Both leaders are charged with unbelief concerning showing God holy and will not lead this assembly into the land. No additional motive is inserted.
Water of Dispute translates the selected designation, followed by reviling and divine sanctification among them.
Moses' messengers address Edom's king as Israel's brother and appeal to known hardship.
The fathers' descent, the people's long sojourn and Egyptian mistreatment of both generations remain.
The Lord hears, sends an angel and brings them out; Kadesh is described at the territory's edge. No angel identity is supplied.
The proposed royal-road passage excludes fields, vineyards, cistern water and turning right or left until beyond the borders.
Edom refuses passage and threatens war if it occurs. The personified through me remains.
The selected route is alongside the mountain, repeated twice; payment is offered if people or livestock drink. No highway/feet alternative is substituted.
Refusal repeats, followed by a large force and strong hand. The military force is kept distinct from the strength image.
Edom's unwillingness causes Israel to turn away rather than forcing passage.
Departure from Kadesh brings the entire assembly to Mount Hor.
The Lord addresses Moses and Aaron at Hor on Edom's border.
Aaron is gathered to his people; the selected non-entry and provocation verbs address both leaders in the plural. Water of Reviling differs lexically from verse 13's designation.
Aaron and Eleazar ascend before the whole congregation under Moses' direction.
Aaron's robe transfers to Eleazar before Aaron's gathering and death. The selected imperatives remain.
Moses obeys and brings him up, retaining the singular object despite the two men named in the command.
Moses strips Aaron and clothes Eleazar; Aaron dies at the summit, and Moses and Eleazar descend. The succession and agents remain clear.
Released preserves the selected death euphemism. All Israel mourns thirty days, with the number and whole-house scope retained.
